description:
More than 130 years later, the Lizzie Borden case remains one of America’s most famous unsolved murder mysteries.

This video explores 50 of the strangest facts surrounding the brutal 1892 killings of Andrew and Abby Borden. From Lizzie’s questionable alibi and changing statements to the mysterious hatchet, burned clothing, alleged poison purchase, and evidence police may have overlooked, nearly every part of the case raises new questions.
We also examine alternative suspects, the role of Victorian attitudes toward women, the weaknesses of the investigation, and why an all-male jury acquitted Lizzie so quickly. After the trial, Lizzie inherited a fortune, moved into the mansion she had always wanted, and lived the rest of her life under a cloud of suspicion.

Even the famous nursery rhyme got the details wrong. So what actually happened inside the Borden house?

description:
North Korea didn’t begin with Kim Il Sung. Its story stretches back thousands of years through ancient kingdoms, Mongol invasions, royal dynasties, Japanese occupation, civil war, and one of the most dramatic political divisions in modern history.

This video takes you through 5,000 years of Korean history, from the legendary founding of Gojoseon and the rise of Goguryeo to the Goryeo and Joseon dynasties. Along the way, Korea faced Khitan armies, Mongol conquest, Japanese invasions, Manchu domination, Western gunboats, and an accelerating struggle between China, Russia, Japan, and the United States for influence over the peninsula. Then came Japanese annexation in 1910, decades of colonial rule, forced labor, cultural suppression, and resistance. After Japan’s defeat in 1945, Korea was divided along the 38th parallel between Soviet and American occupation zones. That temporary division became permanent.
